A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BLOCK-EM study. The main text and Appendices A-F are readable, and their equations, table, and figures can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, cross-domain evaluations, latent-selection ablations, and activation-patching results in Sections 4-5 and Appendices C-F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations on two additional models and comparisons with prompting and steering baselines.

M1.justification: The three-stage latent-discovery procedure and base-anchored, sign-aware blocking objective remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. The additional model experiments instantiate the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Finance/Health experiments, six transfer domains, and core misalignment and final evaluation prompt suites. The additional model evaluations reuse this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The external comparison expands beyond KL regularization to inoculation prompting, preventative steering, and test-time steering. Figure 7 includes linear-probe steering, while Figure 19 additionally displays SAE-based steering. Existing random-latent and Top-Delta controls are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds full-pipeline evaluations on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, using model-matched SAEs and separately rediscovered latent sets. These substantially expand the tested model configurations; the original splits, metrics, and training defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The latent-source, set-size, directionality, freezing, final-layer, reconstruction, and activation-patching analyses are retained. Matching Appendices D-F shows that their figures and findings are moved or renumbered, rather than newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and uncertainty conventions are retained, including three-seed standard-deviation reporting and six-domain SEM reporting. The new model plots use the existing two-seed, six-domain SEM convention; no new statistical testing or uncertainty procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 7 and 19 add comparator results, and new Figures 20-21 report model-specific trade-offs. At lambda = 100,000, the latter show approximately 40% relative misalignment reduction for Llama-3.2-1B and 65% for Qwen-2.5-7B. These are additional settings and results, not improved scores for the original Llama-3.1 experiment.

T1.justification: The SAE definitions, latent-selection scores, blocking-loss formulation, and patching mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are added or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about targeted suppression, cross-domain transfer, task preservation, and failure under prolonged training. The additional experiments broaden support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: The mechanistic interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the H1-H3 discussion, evidence favoring incomplete coverage at the blocking layer, and qualifications on activation-patching conclusions. The additional comparisons and model curves introduce findings rather than new mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the additional models' SAE sources through EleutherAI and Arditi references and explains that discovery is repeated separately. It removes the original Goodfire SAE and Llama-3.1 resource references and the explicit KL-objective display. Shared hyperparameters and the code link remain, but new comparator configurations receive limited detail.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Wichers et al. on inoculation and Chen et al. on preventative steering, explicitly distinguishing BLOCK-EM from these interventions. SAE-source references are added, while the LoRA, Goodfire, and Llama-3.1 model references are removed. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'by Blocking Causal Features' to 'via Latent Blocking.' Related-work, setup, and comparison paragraphs receive localized revisions, and acknowledgments and an impact statement are added. Most prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset into an ICML format, changing typography, running headers, captions, spacing, and figure placement throughout. Figures 7 and 19 gain comparator series, Figure 19's axis range expands, and two model-replication figures are added. Most existing graphics and Table 1 retain their content.

improvement.justification: v1's external-defense comparison centers on KL regularization, and its experiments use one base model. v2 adds relevant prompting and steering comparisons plus model-specific replications on two further backbones, substantially strengthening evidence about comparative value and generality. Sparse configuration details and lost resource references limit reproducibility, but these documentation weaknesses do not outweigh the broader empirical validation.
